summary: This note is a wiki-style article on the United States Virgin Islands, a Caribbean territory of the United States. It covers the territory's political history, from its transfer from Denmark in 1916 through its constitutional conventions and the rejected 2009 Constitution, along with its main islands, land area, and capital. It also gives the territory's official name and its geographic location in the Leeward Islands.
one_line: Overview of the United States Virgin Islands, a Caribbean U.S. territory with its constitutional history, islands, area, and capital.
key_facts: The United States Virgin Islands were previously the Danish West Indies of the Kingdom of Denmark-Norway.
Denmark sold the Danish West Indies to the United States in the Treaty of the Danish West Indies of 1916.
The U.N. classifies the U.S. Virgin Islands as a Non-Self-Governing Territory.
The U.S. Virgin Islands are organized under the 1954 Revised Organic Act of the Virgin Islands.
The territory has held five constitutional conventions.
The Fifth Constitutional Convention of the U.S. Virgin Islands adopted a proposed Constitution in 2009, which was the last and only proposed Constitution.
The U.S. Congress rejected the proposed Constitution in 2010 and urged the convention to reconvene.
The Fifth Constitutional Convention met in October 2012 but did not produce a revised Constitution before its October 31 deadline.
The main islands of the U.S. Virgin Islands are Saint Croix, Saint John, and Saint Thomas, along with many surrounding minor islands.
The total land area of the territory is 133.73 square miles (346.36 km).
The territory's capital is Charlotte Amalie on the island of Saint Thomas.
The United States Virgin Islands are also called the American Virgin Islands.
The official name is the Virgin Islands of the United States.
The islands are located in the Leeward Islands of the Lesser Antilles in the Caribbean.
The U.S. Virgin Islands are an unincorporated and organized territory of the United States.
